ui: Car and work have separate avatar areas; task fill grows gradually. House room tiles show linked completion fill and open room details. SSD delivery is shown 10:30 AM–2:30 PM Monday–Saturday through Dec 26; backpack checks are scheduled after the latest child pickup in the first free slot, and stale morning reminders are repaired. Cleared project actions stay cleared, sync conflicts pause automatic overwrites for review, the Money account-exit checklist now uses working tap controls, Spirituality shortcuts keep consistent full-page navigation, and Money distinguishes linked accounts from budget-mapped accounts and separates balance dates from connection sync dates, and blocks confirmed-closed checking from available-cash mapping, and preserves subscription payment and renewal details across sync, and shows an estimated renewal separately from confirmed bills, and rejects generic bank fees as bill matches. Version reporting now uses one build identifier across startup, system health, and the update check. Budget now distinguishes no bills due this month from no bills saved, and the Accounts empty state explains when synced accounts still need Money mapping. Spirituality journal saves and daily-practice toggles now restore the previous state and show an error if the local save fails. Money now surfaces possible monthly charges from repeated posted transactions, labels them as estimates, and keeps them separate from saved bills and cash forecasts. The monthly-payment review also surfaces variable-amount patterns with observed ranges, while keeping all candidates outside confirmed bill totals. Build identifiers now share one source, service-worker cache versions follow the registered build, and cloud snapshot writes verify the live release before accepting data. Friday Dolly dance remains at 5:15 PM, Friday Dad pickup is corrected to about 4:30 PM, and the Nov 6 occurrence notes that Leo and Demitri were picked up Nov 5. On SSD driver delivery days, Daily Flow omits the home-from-UPS shower block and auto-scheduled home/school chores before and during the route; hydration reminders remain visible. Habit building is now available across the life areas: Today gathers active habits, each area page shows its own habits, and users can add, log, edit, pause, or resume habits. Practice history is saved in the existing local/cloud snapshot; appointments and one-time tasks remain separate. The Today all-area habit view is now the default starting page. Habit reminders can be enabled per habit as a timed 14-day phone-notification trial; reminders stop after the trial and skip days already logged. Growth & Hobbies now includes a 19-doll Monster High starter catalog with real product photos, generation/search/ownership filters for Michelle and Dolly, and a custom-doll form. The expanded catalog includes G3 Venus, alternate Venus releases, the Love in Scaris Garrott du Roque and Rochelle Goyle two-pack, and distinct Draculaura releases. Ownership selections sync in the existing snapshot. Family home now keeps vertical scrolling enabled on phones. The app update check now reads the shared APP_BUILD constant, and the service-worker asset list has valid JavaScript so the Monster High files install and refresh with the app. A visible Monster High dolls shortcut now appears in the Garden + Hobbies open-sections area, where it opens the collection tracker. The Hobby Projects drawer now has a dedicated Monster High collection card with an Open tracker button. The external archive button is removed from the tracker; doll browsing and custom entries stay in Daily Life. The Love in Scaris two-pack is now listed as separate Garrott du Roque and Rochelle Goyle cards with independent ownership checkboxes. The shared app shell now preserves vertical touch scrolling across phone pages, including Home, instead of limiting scrolling to selected views. Monster High ownership changes now wait for the local save and attempt an immediate guarded cloud snapshot push, avoiding a refresh race with the delayed background sync. Monster High collection sync now merges timestamped ownership from cloud and preserves the collection against older full-snapshot writes. Habit reminders now stay active until turned off instead of expiring after a 14-day trial; the server dispatcher accepts ongoing schedules. App updates now wait for a clear Reload now choice instead of force-reloading open tabs as soon as a new service worker installs; saved work stays available while an update waits. The offline app worker now keeps the current version if a required core file cannot download, and the update check blocks a release dated earlier than the installed build. The service worker now caches all current page scripts and stylesheets, including household maps and reading/task helpers, for more complete offline use. A small save-status strip now shows local, syncing, cloud-synced, offline, or review-needed state and opens Cloud settings. A one-tap Workday focus button shows today’s UPS/SSD route blocks and the next scheduled commitment without household chore lists. Workday focus now selects the next scheduled event rather than surfacing a chore as the next commitment. Habit check-ins are now reachable from a compact strip across the app, and saved task, water, habit, and Day Flow completions get a brief positive checkmark animation. Habit progress now appears in a compact check-in strip throughout the app, with Done and Partly actions, a daily progress bar, and a gentle saved-completion toast. The Monster High catalog now includes 10 additional releases with official Mattel product photos, bringing the starter list to 32, with Toralei Stripe Creeproduction and Sweet Screams Twyla. Hobby project cards have separate Start, Finish, Resume, and Restart controls. The Hobbies workspace has one-tap project starters for beginner yoga, a first kombucha batch, and crafting; they create editable project drafts only when Michelle chooses to save them. Hobby projects now have separate Start, Finish, Resume, and Restart controls for quick progress updates. Monster High catalog navigation now loads after the expanded entries were corrected. Ownership merges now resolve Michelle and Dolly’s checkboxes per doll and per owner using change timestamps, so a newer mark or unmark survives snapshot merges instead of an unrelated later change replacing the collection. App update reload now has a timed recovery path if service worker activation does not send a controller-change event, preventing the “Reloading…” panel from remaining stuck. When no active habits exist, the one-time starter migration adds the two requested practices—drinking water and brushing teeth—so they appear in the habit builder and quick check-in strip. On usual Tuesday–Saturday workdays, Day Flow now reserves the workday and school-pickup window, moves household tasks to 3:30 PM or later, and keeps early tasks out of the timeline. Day Flow buttons now have larger phone tap targets. Water and brushing-teeth starter habits turn on recurring reminders by default (7:00 AM water, 7:30 PM teeth); reminders remain active until turned off, and the push service now treats a blank end date as ongoing. Workday delivery remains open-ended through the fixed 2:52 PM school pickup; Tanner is listed as fallback if the route is still active. On today’s workday, home tasks stay hidden until home arrival is confirmed in Workday focus; future workdays keep the 3:30 PM earliest home-task time. Starter water stays at 7:00 AM mid-shift, and the built-in 7:30 PM teeth reminder is corrected to 4:00 AM before work. Hobby rotation now starts Monday, Nov 16, includes an optional handmade Christmas or birthday gift goal, and waits to offer session logging until then. SSD weekly estimates now appear in Money → Income, separate hourly wages from per-mile pay, and keep missing shift details unknown. Fixed the Life Map startup crash caused by using money goal progress before it was initialized; corrected the error-screen build label to match the current app version. Life Map’s avatar now has large tappable regions for its existing area panels, with keyboard support for focused regions. The figure now wears pants instead of a skirt; saved data and tracking remain unchanged. The app’s offline shell now includes the Life Map script and styles. The Life Map avatar now opens its area panel through delegated touch and keyboard events and scrolls the result into view. Today’s plan clearly shows a completed-task count and opens the Today list. Habit check-ins no longer appear at the top of every page; they remain in the dedicated Today/habits area. The save banner now calls out that the cloud copy is pending. Life Map avatar taps now open and scroll to their matching area; Today’s tasks opens the task list. The global habit check-in strip is removed from the top of general pages, while habit logging remains available on Today and area pages. Sync wording now distinguishes a local phone save from a pending cloud copy. This is a UI-only update; existing phone data is preserved. Tapping any Life Map avatar hotspot or area card now opens its own full-page Life Map area view with related tasks, last completed activity, and a route to its existing tracker. A Back to Life Map control returns to the main map. This is a UI and navigation update; saved records are unchanged. The Today shortcut inside a Life Map area now opens a filtered page containing tasks linked only to that area; it no longer opens the all-area habit view. The Money page labels its budget as unfinished until income and funded categories are set up. The Life Map now keeps only the clickable avatar instead of repeating all six areas as cards with progress bars. The pants start pale and fill from the bottom up as completed money goals and money tasks progress. The Life Map character now has a cuter face and outfit details. The house floor plan uses matching pastel styling, room photos are hidden from the map and appear only after opening a room. Repeated copies of the Volvo key task now appear once under Car & driving, not Work; its completed history remains intact. Confirmed closed Wells Fargo checking and savings are hidden from active linked accounts while history remains; deposit closure matching includes savings. Go2bank account type can be shown as Michelle's savings override. Weekly UPS schedule now has a Sunday shift review, a Wednesday accuracy check, and date-specific workday overrides with editable scheduled start times; actual punch records remain separate. Today and recurring routine lists show last-completed dates for habits, recurring tasks, and household chores. Schedule photos can be read on-device into the weekly UPS shift editor; OCR results stay editable and are saved only after review. House floors now open as tappable layouts traced from the saved vacuum maps when room outlines are available; room progress stays in its own details section. Automatic cloud snapshots now retry temporary sync failures with backoff and resume on reconnect or when Daily Life returns to view; the save indicator updates when sync fails. Daily habit check-ins now keep unanswered habit questions on screen after each saved answer; the full app refresh waits until all unanswered habits are handled, preventing the first response from dismissing the rest. A Clueless-inspired digital wardrobe foundation now lets you add outfit or clothing photos, label them as a vest, top, bottom, shoes, accessory, or complete outfit, sample their colors only on your device, and apply the matching colors to the cartoon avatar. A saved wardrobe item can be assigned to SSD days. No image-analysis API, subscription, or paid service is used; the exact seasonal helper vest shape can be refined from its photo when provided. Clothing photos selected for the wardrobe can now use a free-tier Gemini vision model to identify garment type, style, silhouette, neckline, sleeves, pattern, material appearance, colors, and visible details. The avatar draws matching vest pockets and seams, hoodie details, shirt collar, and supported patterns; outfit analysis stops at free quota and never calls a paid image-generation model. Connecting requires the user's own free-tier API key, stored in Supabase Vault; selected wardrobe photos are sent to Google, whose free tier may use content to improve products. Photo Inbox adds an optional Equestria Girls-inspired cartoon-copy action powered by AI Horde volunteer GPUs. Selected style photos are sent to the community generator; originals remain saved, results appear as new inbox copies, and anonymous requests may be shared to improve image models. The free queue may take several minutes or be temporarily unavailable; it does not call a paid image API. Wardrobe photos now open in a review step where each item can be renamed, corrected for type, style details and colors, and scheduled by time of day, season, or SSD route before it is saved. Matching scheduled looks automatically appear on the cartoon avatar. The house map now lists saved rooms that are not yet placed on the drawing as compact tappable links, and the third-floor tab keeps its correct floor name. The Life Map now has a single tappable Today’s task list entry with completed and open counts. The Life Map now prioritizes the clickable house drawing and removes the repeated room progress card grid; detailed setup remains in the full House page. Wardrobe schedules refresh while Daily Life remains open and when it returns to focus; a manual Wear choice stays in effect for the current part of the day. First- and second-floor house maps now retain saved vacuum outlines, place any missing rooms from the confirmed layout, and make both stair connections tappable. Life Map now uses Michelle’s full-body Equestria Girls-inspired avatar, keeps clickable life-area hotspots and progress fills, and applies scheduled wardrobe colors to the illustrated outfit. The Life Map now uses Michelle’s face-guided, teal-clad pony avatar with transparent background.
data_version: Digital wardrobe item colors, types, and SSD outfit selection are stored in the existing settings snapshot. Existing photos, tasks, habits, inventory, and cloud records are unchanged. Wardrobe garment-analysis results sync in settings; the optional Google API key stays in encrypted Supabase Vault. Cartoon copies are stored as new photo-inbox rows; original uploads remain unchanged. Each wardrobe item can now store daypart, season, and SSD usage rules alongside its reviewed garment details. Manual wardrobe selections store a date and daypart override in existing settings.
